 Oral Judgment
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant challenging by the judgment dated 01.09.2018 passed by the
Additional District Judge and Additional Mact, Udupi (Sitting at Kundapura), Kundapura, in Mvc
No.325/2017.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 01.02.2016 at about 5.30 p.m.,
the claimant being pedestrian while walking on the very side of the road near Margoli of Basrur Village, at that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Temporary Registration No.KA.20.NT007343/2016-17 came from Kundapura side NC: 2024:KHC:37686 towards Basrur side driven by the rider in a very high speed and rash and negligent manner came to wrong side and dashed to the claimant.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and NC: 2024:KHC:37686 award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.1,23,930/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.

Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been Minor Arpitha Shetty vs Mr Raghavendra on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118481123/
2 filed.
6.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the claimant has submitted that the claimant has sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
She examined the doctor as PW-2.
The doctor in his evidence has deposed that the claimant suffered 12% disability in respect of her right leg.
She has produced medical bills amounting to Rs.18,932/-.
Even after discharge from the hospital, she was not in a position to discharge her regular work.
She has suffered lot of pain during treatment.
Considering the same, the compensation of Rs.1,23,932/- granted by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Hence, he sought to allow the appeal.
On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that at the time of the accident, the claimant was a minor and she was non- earning member of the family.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and medical records, the Tribunal has granted just and reasonable compensation and it does not call for interference.
Hence, he sought to dismissal the appeal.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9. It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the accident occurred on 01.02.2016 due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider.

10. As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained right ankle deformed tendon lateral aspect fractural lateral mallelous, abrasion over right elbow, tendon occipital NC: 2024:KHC:37686 region and abrasion over right ankle.

She has produced medical bills amounting to Rs.18,932/-.
11.
At the time of the accident, the claimant was aged about 11 years and was studying in the 7th standard.
The doctor in his evidence has deposed that the claimant suffered 12% disability in respect of her right leg.
As a result of the accident, the claimant was unable to perform her daily activities and her further studies were adversely affected.

The Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.8572/2018 disposed of on 04.11.2022 has held that the decision of Apex Court in the case of Mallikarjun -v- Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd and others reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396 cannot be construed to be laying down the straight jacket formulae.

In view of the above, considering the evidence of the claimant, nature of injuries mentioned in the wound certificate and medical records, I am of the opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, Rs.1,23,932/-, NC: 2024:KHC:37686 should be enhanced to Rs.2,23,932/- with interest at 6% per annum.
13. In the result, the following order is passed:
